title: SubDyve: Subgraph-Driven Dynamic Propagation for Virtual Screening Enhancement Controlling False Positive
claim: A staged network-based method builds a substructure-aware graph, then iteratively refines seeds with false-discovery control before final ranking.
layout: 2 stacked panels (A overview, B zoom-in), left-to-right, nested dashed iteration loop
description: Two stacked panels with black arrows flowing left to right. Panel A is the overall workflow. Labeled (red) and unlabeled (blue) compound-library cylinders feed subgraph pattern mining and fingerprint matrices drawn as red and blue heatmap strips. These build a subgraph-fingerprint similarity network, a node-link graph. The network feeds a green dotted box, 'Dynamic seed refinement with LFDR', then a decaying red-gradient curve for prioritizing compounds. Brackets underneath label each stage. Panel B zooms into the green box. It shows N stratified seed splits and a graph with orange seed nodes. Stacked green feature-encoding blocks feed a GNN. An inner dashed loop of M iterations has an LFDR density plot and propagation and evaluation, with curved blue arrows. The result is a best seed weight bar, ensembled over N runs, then final network propagation.
caption: Architecture of SubDyve Framework. (A) Overall process of SubDyve. Consists of subgraph-similariy network construction, dynamic seed refinement with LFDR, and prioritization. (B) Dynamic seed refinement with LFDR: seed weights are iteratively updated within each stratified split and aggregated for final prioritization.
abstract: Virtual screening (VS) aims to identify bioactive compounds from vast chemical libraries, but remains difficult in low-label regimes where only a few actives are known. Existing methods largely rely on general-purpose molecular fingerprints and overlook class-discriminative substructures critical to bioactivity. Moreover, they consider molecules independently, limiting effectiveness in low-label regimes. We introduce SubDyve, a network-based VS framework that constructs a subgraph-aware similarity network and propagates activity signals from a small known actives. When few active compounds are available, SubDyve performs iterative seed refinement, incrementally promoting new candidates based on local false discovery rate. This strategy expands the seed set with promising candidates while controlling false positives from topological bias and overexpansion. We evaluate SubDyve on ten DUD-E targets under zero-shot conditions and on the CDK7 target with a 10-million-compound ZINC dataset. SubDyve consistently outperforms existing fingerprint or embedding-based approaches, achieving margins of up to +34.0 on the BEDROC and +24.6 on the EF1% metric.
